summary: An excerpt from a science fiction novel (labeled Book 15, part 15) in which Ray Marlowe is summoned to the captain's ready room aboard the starship Paraclete. Captain Sorensen, seated at the conference table and staring at a recessed terminal, confronts Ray with irritation over his defiance of orders, while Becker, who guides Ray to his chair, prepares drinks at the wet bar. The scene establishes the room's refined, spartan decor and its transparent wall showing the star field.
one_line: Ray Marlowe is confronted by irritated Captain Sorensen in the Paraclete's ready room over his disobeyed orders.
key_facts: The passage is titled "Book 15 — part 15" and is categorized under the source "books" in the fiction domain.
Paraclete is styled as the most secure passenger liner in the history of human transport.
Ray exits the lift and takes a left hand turn away from the main bridge, entering a door without knocking.
Becker is holding the door ajar when Ray arrives and gives him a look that might be relief or a you are such a tool sentiment.
The captain's ready room has a polished mahogany table with comfortable cloth chairs in the center.
The opposite wall of the ready room is a single sheet of industrial plastisheen, stronger than flexsteel but completely transparent.
Sorensen's massive antique desk has been modified to contain the latest model data terminal.
A wide mirror mounts the expansive wet bar so Sorensen can mix drinks without breaking eye contact with guests.
Sorensen sits at the conference table rather than behind his desk.
Becker guides Ray into the nearest chair, which is opposite the captain.
Sorensen peers through a clouded glass window at a recessed terminal screen and does not acknowledge Ray's arrival.
Sorensen asks Ray, "Why are you such a pain in my ass, Marlowe?"
Sorensen asks whether Ray wants a drink, saying "I want a drink."
Ray accepts with a nod, and Becker crosses to the bar to prepare the drinks, including scotch straight and vodka with lime.
